text: water; insoluble in alcohol. The pH of a 5% solution in water is not less than 2.9. Profile Aluminium sulfate has an action similar to that of alum (p.2254) but is more astringent. A 20% solution is used for the treatment of envenomation by certain insects and marine organisms. The aluminium may cause precipitation of the proteins contained within the venoms thus reducing local toxicity. Aluminium sul- fate is also included in astringent preparations intended to soothe irritating skin conditions. Aluminium sulfate is also used in the preparation of aluminium acetate solutions. Adverse effects. Possible adverse effects or toxicity associated with aluminium, or aluminium salts such as aluminium sulfate, in the public water supply are discussed under Aluminium, p.2254. Preparations USP 31: Aluminum Subacetate Topical Solution; Aluminum Sulfate and Calcium Acetate for Topical Solution; Aluminum Sulfate and Calcium Ace- tate Tablets for Topical Solution.
